clue.text: Retro fashions felt intimate behind Collection on show here?

indicators.note: retro means looking backwards, so the word for the felting verb is read from its end

parts.note: to mat hair or fibres is to felt them, so mats means fashions felt
an intimate is a close friend, a pal
behind is a word for the bottom, bum in British slang

explanation.surface: Someone notes that old-fashioned styles felt cosy, set behind a museum collection on display.
explanation.walkthrough: BUM is British slang for the backside. The definition is cryptic: stamps are a collection shown off in this book.
explanation.definitionFit: A philatelist's stamps are kept and displayed in this book, so it is where that collection goes on show.

clue.text: Refuse pay for jobs done around London?

parts.note: SE, the south-east, is the region surrounding London (and a London postal area)
a wage is pay for work done

explanation.surface: Someone declines to accept payment for work done in and around the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewage is waste matter carried off in drains, a kind of refuse.

clue.text: Conflicting notices about upcoming period

indicators.note: about means the notices go round the other piece

parts.note: ads are notices, advertisements

indicators.note: in a down clue, upcoming means the word for period is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a period is a full stop, a dot

explanation.surface: Clashing notices concerning a coming period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at odds is to disagree, so it is an idiom for conflicting.

clue.text: Figure the usual gene was transmitted down the line

parts.note: par is the usual or normal standard
an allele is a form of a gene
piped means sent through a pipe or line

explanation.surface: A typical gene was handed down through the family line.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests heredity; 'Figure' is a solid shape in geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a solid geometric figure with six parallelogram faces.

clue.text: Protection for audience Boult cryptically supplied?

definitions.text: Protection for audience Boult cryptically supplied?

parts.words: Protection for audience Boult cryptically supplied?
parts.note: Heard by an audience his surname is the bolt that strikes in a storm, and the rod guarding a building from it shares his job title

explanation.surface: Something shielding a concert audience, provided by Sir Adrian Boult in a puzzling way.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Adrian Boult was a famous British orchestral conductor. Heard aloud, Boult is bolt, so a lightning bolt's conductor is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal rod that carries lightning strikes safely to earth protects a building; Boult was a conductor, pun intended.

clue.text: Greatly affect author, overwriting map of hill country

indicators.note: overwriting means one word is written over another, replacing it

parts.note: upland is high, hilly country
a plan is a map or diagram
to pen is to write, so pen stands for author

explanation.surface: A writer's work changes how a map of the hills is drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend someone's life is to overturn it, figuratively to affect them greatly.

clue.text: Fine location for researching blubber?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a lab is a place where research is done

explanation.surface: A good place to do research on whale fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Flab is loose surplus body fat, much as blubber is.

clue.text: Who's eating sandwiches at timeless Nasa installation?

indicators.note: sandwiches means the eater holds the other piece between its letters

parts.note: a luncher is someone eating lunch

indicators.note: timeless means the word at loses its T, the time abbreviation

explanation.surface: Asking who is munching sandwiches at a space centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food, fitting the eating; it is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A launcher is the rig or rocket system from which space vehicles are sent up.

clue.text: Spooner's old man puts money on write-offs!

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: old man is slang for father, dad
bets means wagers money on; said aloud it is the same as the word with a silent B after its E, which is how the swap is spelt

explanation.surface: A father gambling on things that end up being written off.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of DAD BETS gives 'bad dets', which is spoken just like the phrase with the silent B in debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Debts that will never be repaid are written off in accounts, so they are write-offs.

clue.text: Orthodox teen stopping by at intervals for dalliance?

indicators.note: stopping means the two letters of by plug gaps among the rearranged letters of the orthodox teen
at intervals says the letters of by go in at separate points, so the whole lot ends up mixed

parts.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A conventional teenager calls round now and then for a flirtation.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ORTHODOX TEEN are rearranged, with B and Y slotted in at different places; the parse shows all of them as one mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The familiar, wholesome young neighbour is the classic object of a romance or flirtation.

clue.text: Bertie now out of the way, is he after Madeline Bassett?

indicators.note: out of means the way's letters are removed

parts.note: Bertie Wooster is P. G. Wodehouse's hero
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: With Bertie now gone, is someone else chasing Madeline Bassett?
explanation.walkthrough: In Wodehouse, Madeline Bassett is the soppy girl Bertie Wooster dreads being engaged to.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor courting a woman is a wooer, someone pursuing her.

clue.text: Breeder's output, say, uranium fuelling atomisation of hydrogen

indicators.note: fuelling means the uranium is fed into the other letters
atomisation breaks something into pieces, so the word's letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A breeder reactor's product, with uranium powering the splitting of hydrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: The nuclear surface makes 'Breeder' a reactor; here it is a dog breeder.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog breeder produces puppies, and a racing greyhound is one example of such output.

clue.text: Time for believers to view gallery collection?

parts.note: the gods is the highest gallery in a theatre
a lot is a collection, as in an auction

explanation.surface: Visiting time for the faithful to see an art gallery's holdings.
explanation.walkthrough: The gods is the theatre's top gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcasting slot reserved for religious programmes is the idiom for the believers' airtime.

clue.text: This fiasco would be predictable with trip so badly organised

indicators.note: badly organised means the letters of predictable are jumbled, with those of trip set aside

explanation.surface: A disaster that would be foreseeable if a trip were poorly arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of the answer plus TRIP rearrange to make PREDICTABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden humiliating failure, a fiasco.

clue.text: Fed peanuts, regulars among guests become restless

indicators.note: fed means the payment is put inside the selected letters
regulars picks out every other letter of guests

parts.note: peanuts means a tiny payment, a titchy fee

explanation.surface: After eating peanuts, regular visitors among the guests get fidgety.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of guests give GET; TITCHY FEE, British slang for a tiny fee, goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To get itchy feet is an idiom for wanting to move on or travel, being restless.

clue.text: See 4
Top Chinese meal sent up literally represses obsession

indicators.note: represses means the literally letters hold the reversed pieces down inside them

parts.note: IE, id est, means that is, or literally

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: Xi Jinping is China's top leader
a feed is a meal

explanation.surface: A senior Chinese figure's dinner, mocked, literally holding back a fixation.
explanation.walkthrough: Xi Jinping heads China. 'literally' stands for i.e. (that is), which works only loosely: both introduce a restatement.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase means a fixed idea, a fixation that dominates the mind.

clue.text: Liking a piano pretty small

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
petite means small and dainty

explanation.surface: Fondness for a rather small piano.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetite for something is a desire or taste for it.

clue.text: Double parking in German motor garage initially cuts risk

indicators.note: cuts means these letters slice into the risk word

parts.note: danger is risk

indicators.note: in places the parking letter inside the car

parts.note: Opel is a German car maker

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of garage

explanation.surface: Twice the risk of parking in a German car garage.
explanation.definitionFit: A doppelganger is someone's exact lookalike, their double.

clue.text: Taken up from dugout, is nicely positioned

indicators.note: Taken up says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone lifted from a dugout is sitting comfortably.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hidden step no indicator; 'from' is that signal, telling you to take the letters out of 'dugout, is nicely'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in its original place, so it describes something positioned where it belongs.

clue.text: Wound wife is probing with spike

indicators.note: is probing means the wife letter pushes inside the spiked word

parts.note: tined means having tines or spikes, like a fork

explanation.surface: A wife probes a wound with a sharp spike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like an injury, but it is the past tense of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Twined means twisted or coiled around, as a cord is wound.

clue.text: Sorrowful career-girl drifting without learning basics

indicators.note: drifting means the letters wander into a new order
without says some letters are left out of the mix

parts.note: the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are the basics of learning

explanation.surface: A sad career woman drifts along with no grounding in the fundamentals.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are a traditional name for basic schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac means mournful, in the manner of an elegy for the dead.

clue.text: Part of lunch: an Asian foodstuff?

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A component of a midday meal: something Asian to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Chana is the chickpea, a staple ingredient in South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Doing not the first jot of work thus far

parts.note: up to means doing, as in what are you up to
no means not

indicators.note: the first jot of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone has done no work at all so far.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means until now, so far in time.

clue.text: What the Doctor ordered in books about time traveller

parts.note: just what the doctor ordered is it, the very thing
an era is a period of time
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: A prescription in books about Doctor Who, the time traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time traveller' calls up Doctor Who, but only traveller defines; 'about' simply links, meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerant is someone who moves from place to place, a wanderer.

clue.text: On reflection, it's not possible to keep current Head

indicators.note: on reflection means the whole is mirrored, read backwards
to keep means the no-no holds the current letter

parts.note: a no-no is something not possible or not allowed
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Thinking again, a head cannot hold the flow of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Onion is old slang for the head, as in 'off your onion'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the head is called an onion, as in being off one's onion.

clue.text: It's parting day, for the poet quits

definitions.text: It's parting day, for the poet
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the poetic word for ..., the day's departure

explanation.surface: A poet declares that the day is departing and gives up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the knell of parting day' is Gray's line about evening in his Elegy; poets shorten evening to this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people who are quits have settled up and are level; poets also use the word for nightfall.

clue.text: Where the rides are just fine!

parts.note: fair means just
ground means crushed fine, like coffee

explanation.surface: Where the rides are, which is simply fine!
explanation.walkthrough: 'rides' and 'fine' combine into a passing remark; 'fine' is ground as in powdered.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground is the open site of a funfair with its carousels and roller coasters.
